The trial court should rule the testimony **D, inadmissible because the company did not have the opportunity to cross-examine the engineer on the liability issue**. I'm choosing D over C because it names the specific flaw in the former-testimony exception. The company deposed him in a wrongful-termination suit, so it had no similar motive to develop his testimony on whether the aircraft were defective. That fails the "similar motive" requirement of FRE 804(b)(1), so the testimony is hearsay with no applicable exception. I'm revising my earlier answer of A, which I now think overlooked the motive requirement.

CONFIDENCE: 70
